load.title: Meet the rotor
load.instruction: Welcome to the wheel lab. Your mission is to make a spacecraft rotor shake less. A tiny off-center mass pulls outward each turn, causing vibration.
load.science: We'll measure it, add known test masses, then cancel the shake. Grip the tray rotor and seat it upright on the spindle.
load.text: Welcome to the wheel lab. Your mission is to make a spacecraft rotor shake less. A tiny off-center mass pulls outward each turn, causing vibration. We'll measure it, add known test masses, then cancel the shake. Grip the tray rotor and seat it upright on the spindle.

home.title: Reference the probe
home.instruction: Press Home on the station to set the probe's reference position at six millimeters.
home.science: This sensor measures tiny vibration without touching the rotor. Before comparing measurements, we need a repeatable distance between sensor and target.
home.text: Press Home on the station to set the probe's reference position at six millimeters. This sensor measures tiny vibration without touching the rotor. Before comparing measurements, we need a repeatable distance between sensor and target.

probe_adjust.title: Try the micrometer
probe_adjust.instruction: Use the right stick to reach the station's right side. Grip the micrometer drum, turn to change its reading by a tenth of a millimeter, then release.
probe_adjust.science: Regrip as needed. One revolution moves half a millimeter.
probe_adjust.text: Use the right stick to reach the station's right side. Grip the micrometer drum, turn to change its reading by a tenth of a millimeter, then release. Regrip as needed. One revolution moves half a millimeter.

probe_restore.title: Restore the reference
probe_restore.instruction: Release the micrometer before pressing Home to restore six millimeters. We'll keep that probe position fixed.
probe_restore.science: Sensor motion changes sensitivity and discards calibration. Comparing vibration requires the same measurement setup, so rehome before starting our experiment.
probe_restore.text: Release the micrometer before pressing Home to restore six millimeters. We'll keep that probe position fixed. Sensor motion changes sensitivity and discards calibration. Comparing vibration requires the same measurement setup, so rehome before starting our experiment.

open_setup.title: Open for the dial experiment
open_setup.instruction: At zero speed, lift the orange guard if it is closed. We'll adjust rotor weights next.
open_setup.science: Mass changes require open access and a stopped rotor. Closing the enclosure instead prepares the station for spinning.
open_setup.text: At zero speed, lift the orange guard if it is closed. We'll adjust rotor weights next. Mass changes require open access and a stopped rotor. Closing the enclosure instead prepares the station for spinning.

mass_practice.title: Try the mass dial
mass_practice.instruction: With the rotor stopped and the guard open, grip the Mass dial. Twist to add at least five hundredths of a gram, then release.
mass_practice.science: This changes the size of the correction weight on the selected plane.
mass_practice.text: With the rotor stopped and the guard open, grip the Mass dial. Twist to add at least five hundredths of a gram, then release. This changes the size of the correction weight on the selected plane.

angle_practice.title: Aim the correction weight
angle_practice.instruction: Grip the Angle dial and turn the nonzero weight at least twenty degrees, then release.
angle_practice.science: Mass sets how much correction you add; angle sets where around the rotor it acts. Those two values describe a correction vector.
angle_practice.text: Grip the Angle dial and turn the nonzero weight at least twenty degrees, then release. Mass sets how much correction you add; angle sets where around the rotor it acts. Those two values describe a correction vector.

clear_mass.title: Restore the bare rotor
clear_mass.instruction: Grip Mass and twist back to zero grams, then release. Let go and regrip for extra turns if needed. Leave Angle unchanged.
clear_mass.science: With no weight installed, angle creates no force. Our experiment starts with the bare rotor.
clear_mass.text: Grip Mass and twist back to zero grams, then release. Let go and regrip for extra turns if needed. Leave Angle unchanged. With no weight installed, angle creates no force. Our experiment starts with the bare rotor.

mode_two.title: Choose two-plane balancing
mode_two.instruction: Press Mode to select two-plane balancing.
mode_two.science: A thin disc can often use one correction plane. Our wheel has two separated planes: their weights can cancel both an off-center pull and a rocking effect. We'll measure both sensors.
mode_two.text: Press Mode to select two-plane balancing. A thin disc can often use one correction plane. Our wheel has two separated planes: their weights can cancel both an off-center pull and a rocking effect. We'll measure both sensors.

plane_b.title: Find plane B
plane_b.instruction: Press Plane to select B. Watch which rotor plane is selected.
plane_b.science: The Mass and Angle dials edit only the selected plane. Both planes influence both sensors, so changing B can affect motion measured near A, too.
plane_b.text: Press Plane to select B. Watch which rotor plane is selected. The Mass and Angle dials edit only the selected plane. Both planes influence both sensors, so changing B can affect motion measured near A, too.

plane_a.title: Return to plane A
plane_a.instruction: Press Plane again to return to A. We'll use A for our first known test mass.
plane_a.science: Selecting a plane changes which weight you're editing. It does not add a weight or take a vibration measurement.
plane_a.text: Press Plane again to return to A. We'll use A for our first known test mass. Selecting a plane changes which weight you're editing. It does not add a weight or take a vibration measurement.

speed_explore.title: Explore test speed
speed_explore.instruction: Press Speed to try another test-speed setting. The rotor stays stopped while you choose.
speed_explore.science: A faster rotor produces more force from the same off-center mass. Its support can amplify certain speeds, so consistent test conditions matter.
speed_explore.text: Press Speed to try another test-speed setting. The rotor stays stopped while you choose. A faster rotor produces more force from the same off-center mass. Its support can amplify certain speeds, so consistent test conditions matter.

speed_restore.title: Set the working speed
speed_restore.instruction: Press Speed until the display reads twelve hundred revolutions per minute. The settings cycle through fifteen hundred, nine hundred, and twelve hundred.
speed_restore.science: Keep this working speed for baseline, both trials, and verification to compare their responses.
speed_restore.text: Press Speed until the display reads twelve hundred revolutions per minute. The settings cycle through fifteen hundred, nine hundred, and twelve hundred. Keep this working speed for baseline, both trials, and verification to compare their responses.

guard.title: Close the guard
guard.instruction: Grip the orange handle, lower the guard fully, then release it. Check that the station says closed.
guard.science: The enclosure interlock prevents starting with an open guard. Release the guard, rotor, and dials before any spin.
guard.text: Grip the orange handle, lower the guard fully, then release it. Check that the station says closed. The enclosure interlock prevents starting with an open guard. Release the guard, rotor, and dials before any spin.

preview_start.title: Start a practice spin
preview_start.instruction: Press Sweep to begin a practice spin. Watch the rotor accelerate and the live vibration appear on the monitor.
preview_start.science: This first spin is only for learning the stopping controls. We'll collect our real measurements afterward.
preview_start.text: Press Sweep to begin a practice spin. Watch the rotor accelerate and the live vibration appear on the monitor. This first spin is only for learning the stopping controls. We'll collect our real measurements afterward.

stop.title: Stop the practice spin
stop.instruction: Press Stop and watch the rotor coast to zero. Keep the guard closed until it stops.
stop.science: Stop cancels an unfinished capture. Partly collected data cannot become a trusted calibration point, even when the rotor looked steady.
stop.text: Press Stop and watch the rotor coast to zero. Keep the guard closed until it stops. Stop cancels an unfinished capture. Partly collected data cannot become a trusted calibration point, even when the rotor looked steady.

estop.title: Try the emergency latch
estop.instruction: With the rotor stopped, press the red E-stop. Notice that the emergency state latches.
estop.science: Unlike a routine stop, this also discards calibration. We're practicing at zero speed before collecting data, so no balancing result is lost.
estop.text: With the rotor stopped, press the red E-stop. Notice that the emergency state latches. Unlike a routine stop, this also discards calibration. We're practicing at zero speed before collecting data, so no balancing result is lost.

recover.title: Recover deliberately
recover.instruction: Press Recover at zero speed to release the latch or clear a fault. Another condition may need another press. The rotor stays stopped.
recover.science: Recovery removes the probe reference. Rehome and collect fresh calibration before balancing again.
recover.text: Press Recover at zero speed to release the latch or clear a fault. Another condition may need another press. The rotor stays stopped. Recovery removes the probe reference. Rehome and collect fresh calibration before balancing again.

rehome.title: Reference after recovery
rehome.instruction: Press Home to reference the probe again at six millimeters. Confirm the station is ready with its guard closed.
rehome.science: Recovery is a deliberate sequence: clear the latch, restore the reference, then request a new run.
rehome.text: Press Home to reference the probe again at six millimeters. Confirm the station is ready with its guard closed. Recovery is a deliberate sequence: clear the latch, restore the reference, then request a new run.

baseline.title: Measure the starting shake
baseline.instruction: Press Baseline and watch the time trace. Keep the guard closed through capture, analysis, and coast-down.
baseline.science: Baseline records the starting shake in micrometers peak. Any changed measurement setup needs a fresh baseline.
baseline.text: Press Baseline and watch the time trace. Keep the guard closed through capture, analysis, and coast-down. Baseline records the starting shake in micrometers peak. Any changed measurement setup needs a fresh baseline.

chart_order.title: See the rotation signature
chart_order.instruction: Press Chart to view the order spectrum. Find the markers at one and two.
chart_order.science: One means once per revolution; two means twice. Taller peaks mean larger vibration. Our balancing calculation targets the once-per-turn response.
chart_order.text: Press Chart to view the order spectrum. Find the markers at one and two. One means once per revolution; two means twice. Taller peaks mean larger vibration. Our balancing calculation targets the once-per-turn response.

open_trial.title: Prepare a known change
open_trial.instruction: At zero speed, lift the orange guard handle.
open_trial.science: The baseline tells us how much the station shakes, but not which weight will fix it. A known test mass will reveal how the real measured response changes.
open_trial.text: At zero speed, lift the orange guard handle. The baseline tells us how much the station shakes, but not which weight will fix it. A known test mass will reveal how the real measured response changes.

trial_fit.title: Add the A test mass
trial_fit.instruction: With plane A selected, press Fit Trial. This adds a known quarter-gram test mass relative to the baseline.
trial_fit.science: The helper preserves the original configuration on the other plane. Changing one plane at a time keeps its effect identifiable.
trial_fit.text: With plane A selected, press Fit Trial. This adds a known quarter-gram test mass relative to the baseline. The helper preserves the original configuration on the other plane. Changing one plane at a time keeps its effect identifiable.

close_trial.title: Close for the A trial
close_trial.instruction: Lower the guard fully and release the handle. Keep the A test mass installed.
close_trial.science: Our next run uses the same speed and probe position as baseline. Only the known mass change should explain the new measured response.
close_trial.text: Lower the guard fully and release the handle. Keep the A test mass installed. Our next run uses the same speed and probe position as baseline. Only the known mass change should explain the new measured response.

trial_measure.title: Measure the A response
trial_measure.instruction: Press Measure Trial A and wait for capture, analysis, and coast-down to zero.
trial_measure.science: The difference from baseline shows how a known A-plane mass affects both sensors. Vibration phase describes timing relative to rotation, not simply the heavy spot.
trial_measure.text: Press Measure Trial A and wait for capture, analysis, and coast-down to zero. The difference from baseline shows how a known A-plane mass affects both sensors. Vibration phase describes timing relative to rotation, not simply the heavy spot.

open_trial_b.title: Prepare the second trial
open_trial_b.instruction: At zero speed, lift the guard again. We'll test the other correction plane.
open_trial_b.science: One trial cannot describe both planes independently. Our second known change supplies the missing relationship between the B-plane mass and the two sensors.
open_trial_b.text: At zero speed, lift the guard again. We'll test the other correction plane. One trial cannot describe both planes independently. Our second known change supplies the missing relationship between the B-plane mass and the two sensors.

plane_b_trial.title: Select B for its trial
plane_b_trial.instruction: Press Plane to select B before fitting the second test mass.
plane_b_trial.science: We will compare this trial with the original baseline, not with Trial A. Independent tests let the solver separate the two planes' effects.
plane_b_trial.text: Press Plane to select B before fitting the second test mass. We will compare this trial with the original baseline, not with Trial A. Independent tests let the solver separate the two planes' effects.

trial_fit_b.title: Add the B test mass
trial_fit_b.instruction: Press Fit Trial with B selected. It adds the known quarter-gram test mass on B and restores A to its baseline weight.
trial_fit_b.science: Removing the temporary A trial prevents two simultaneous changes from confusing the calibration.
trial_fit_b.text: Press Fit Trial with B selected. It adds the known quarter-gram test mass on B and restores A to its baseline weight. Removing the temporary A trial prevents two simultaneous changes from confusing the calibration.

close_trial_b.title: Close for the B trial
close_trial_b.instruction: Lower the guard fully and release the handle, keeping the B trial installed.
close_trial_b.science: The two tests must use the same speed, sensor positions, and baseline. Repeatable setup lets us attribute their differences to the known mass changes.
close_trial_b.text: Lower the guard fully and release the handle, keeping the B trial installed. The two tests must use the same speed, sensor positions, and baseline. Repeatable setup lets us attribute their differences to the known mass changes.

trial_measure_b.title: Measure the B response
trial_measure_b.instruction: Press Measure Trial B and wait for capture, analysis, and coast-down to zero.
trial_measure_b.science: Now each known trial has measured responses at both sensors. Together they describe the cross effects needed to predict two correction weights.
trial_measure_b.text: Press Measure Trial B and wait for capture, analysis, and coast-down to zero. Now each known trial has measured responses at both sensors. Together they describe the cross effects needed to predict two correction weights.

solve.title: Predict the correction
solve.instruction: Press Solve. Read the predicted mass and angle for each correction plane on the monitor.
solve.science: The solver combines both measured trial effects to cancel baseline vibration. Poor conditioning means small measurement errors could greatly change that prediction.
solve.text: Press Solve. Read the predicted mass and angle for each correction plane on the monitor. The solver combines both measured trial effects to cancel baseline vibration. Poor conditioning means small measurement errors could greatly change that prediction.

open_apply.title: Open for the correction
open_apply.instruction: At zero speed, lift the guard. Keep the calculated solution available.
open_apply.science: We'll replace the temporary trial with the predicted correction. Leave probe position and speed unchanged: changing the measurement response would invalidate what we just learned.
open_apply.text: At zero speed, lift the guard. Keep the calculated solution available. We'll replace the temporary trial with the predicted correction. Leave probe position and speed unchanged: changing the measurement response would invalidate what we just learned.

apply.title: Install the prediction
apply.instruction: Press Apply Correction with the guard open. Watch both plane weights update to calculated total values.
apply.science: The helper replaces test masses and includes baseline weights correctly. This is a prediction; a fresh measurement must test it.
apply.text: Press Apply Correction with the guard open. Watch both plane weights update to calculated total values. The helper replaces test masses and includes baseline weights correctly. This is a prediction; a fresh measurement must test it.

close_verify.title: Close for the speed checks
close_verify.instruction: Lower the guard fully and release the handle. Keep the calculated weights installed.
close_verify.science: We'll explore their response across speeds, then return to our working speed for verification. That final matched-speed measurement tests the prediction fairly.
close_verify.text: Lower the guard fully and release the handle. Keep the calculated weights installed. We'll explore their response across speeds, then return to our working speed for verification. That final matched-speed measurement tests the prediction fairly.

sweep.title: Explore the speed response
sweep.instruction: Press Sweep and watch the speed-response plot build. Wait for the full sweep and coast-down.
sweep.science: A balanced wheel can still excite support resonance. Next we'll return to twelve hundred revolutions per minute to verify the correction.
sweep.text: Press Sweep and watch the speed-response plot build. Wait for the full sweep and coast-down. A balanced wheel can still excite support resonance. Next we'll return to twelve hundred revolutions per minute to verify the correction.

verify.title: Measure the improvement
verify.instruction: Press Verify and wait through capture, analysis, and coast-down. Compare the new vibration and reported reduction with baseline.
verify.science: A fresh measurement tests the prediction. If reduction is poor, investigate the setup and data rather than declaring success.
verify.text: Press Verify and wait through capture, analysis, and coast-down. Compare the new vibration and reported reduction with baseline. A fresh measurement tests the prediction. If reduction is poor, investigate the setup and data rather than declaring success.

repeat.title: Check the scatter
repeat.instruction: Press Repeat without changing the setup. Wait for three measurement windows and coast-down.
repeat.science: Compare their mean and scatter on the monitor. Repeats show consistency, but cannot reveal shared calibration error. Near zero vibration, phase becomes unreliable.
repeat.text: Press Repeat without changing the setup. Wait for three measurement windows and coast-down. Compare their mean and scatter on the monitor. Repeats show consistency, but cannot reveal shared calibration error. Near zero vibration, phase becomes unreliable.

report.title: Keep the evidence
report.instruction: Press Save Report to preserve your settings, measurements, correction, and diagnostic sweep.
report.science: You've measured a problem, tested known changes, predicted a fix, and checked it. The saved report keeps the evidence so someone else can follow your reasoning.
report.text: Press Save Report to preserve your settings, measurements, correction, and diagnostic sweep. You've measured a problem, tested known changes, predicted a fix, and checked it. The saved report keeps the evidence so someone else can follow your reasoning.
